subdivision_of_building: We would like to demolished the existing garage.
description: DEMOLITION OF EXISTING GARAGE AND ERECTION OF A NEW DETACHED DWELLING HOUSE.
decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - By reason of its combined bulk, massing, design (including use of incongruous material), appearance and introduction of a roof terrace, the proposal results in a discordant, cramped and contrived form of development that fails to be in keeping with the character and appearance of the site and surrounding to the detriment of the visual amenity of the locality, contrary to Policies D3 and D4 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies D12.2 and D12.3 of the Local Plan 2024.

Reason : 2 - By reason of combined bulk, mass, height, depth, proximity to the shared boundary, fenestration and raised terrace, the proposed dwelling would result in an visually obtrusive and dominant form of development to the detriment of the residential amenities nearby occupants, in particular, the occupiers of nos.125 and 126 Ashbourne Road by way of loss of outlook, unreasonable sense of enclosure, overbearing form, noise, loss of privacy and overlooking, the occupiers of no.129 Ashbourne Road by way of loss of privacy, overlooking and noise and the occupiers of no.68 Woodland Way by way of loss of privacy and overlooking, contrary to Policy D6 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies D12.2, D12.3 and D12.4 of the Local Plan 2024.

Reason : 3 - Due to the failure to meet minimum GIA requirements, substandard ceiling heights, lack of cycle parking, inadequate refuse storage, limited light penetration to the proposed bedroom and lack of a justification to fail to provide a step-free access, the layout would result in a poor standard of accommodation for future occupiers and would not provide for accessible housing, contrary to Policies T5 , D6 and D7 of the London Plan 2021.

Reason : 4 - The proposed development fails to provide adequate cycle parking provision in accordance with the London Plan and Merton's Local Plan policies, which seek to promote sustainable modes of transport and reduce reliance on private vehicles. Furthermore, the absence of a completed Section 106 legal agreement to restrict future occupiers from obtaining parking permits within the Controlled Parking Zone would likely result in increased on-street parking pressure, to the detriment of highway safety and the free flow of traffic. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies T1, T5,  T6 and T6.1 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies T16.1, T16.2, T16.3 and T16.4 of the London Plan 2024.

Reason : 5 - In the absence of a Construction Traffic Management Plan, the development has failed to demonstrate that traffic and construction activity would not cause any unacceptable harm to pedestrian, cyclist, and vehicular and road safety, in conflict with Policy D12.11 of the Local Plan 2024.

Reason : 6 - In the absence of detailed drawings showing the distance to the public highway, a Design Statement to confirm that the wall is considered as a retaining wall and reinforced accordingly and to state if highway live load surcharge basement wall has been considered, a construction plan to show details of propping the excavation and formwork until basement wall concrete is fully hardened and an adequate drainage strategy, to include a sustainable urban drainage scheme to reduce runoff rates and implement proposals to conserve and re-use water through rainwater harvesting, or any details relating to the risk of sewer flooding, the submission has failed to demonstrate that the impact of the proposed basement would be acceptable in terms of ground instability issues and drainage considerations, in conflict with Policy D12.11 of the Local Plan 2024.

Reason : 7 - By reason of the scheme failing to achieve Zero Carbon and the absence the Council's Energy Assessment template or overheating calculator, the submission does not identify the level of CO2 reductions beyond the Building regulations baseline that woudl be achieved. Additionally, in the absence of a legal agreement to secure the required carbon offset fund the scheme fails to provide a sustainable and energy efficient scheme contrary to the aims and objectives of policies CC2.1-CC2.4 and CC2.6 of the Local Plan 2024.

Reason : 8 - In the absence of an air quality neutral statement, demonstrating that the proposed development would be air quality neutral, the scheme conflicts with  Policy SI 1 of the London Plan 2021.

Reason : 9 - In the absence of any soft landscaping or planting, or other forms of green infrastructure, the proposed development would not enhance biodiversity, in conflict with Policy O15.3 of the Local Plan 2024.

Reason : 10 - INFORMATIVE
Note to Applicant
In accordance with paragraph 38 of the NPPF, The London Borough of Merton  (LBM) takes a positive and proactive approach to development proposals focused on solutions. LBM works with applicants/agents in a positive and proactive manner by:
"	Offering a pre-application advice and duty desk service. 
"	Where possible, suggesting solutions to secure a successful outcome.
"	As appropriate, updating applicants/agents of any issues that may arise in the processing of their application.
In this instance:
"	The application was not considered to comply with the provisions of the Development Plan and NPPF as submitted, and would have required substantial changes such that a new application would be required.
